items.title: Jane Monheit interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 20, 2010
items.q: the winner of the competition, Terry Thornton, was over 40 years older than I was. She was first and I was second.

ctx.x: It’s interesting, Eric Alexander said — I think he placed second in the Thelonious Monk competition also, behind Joshua Redman. And he said six months later he was working in a cubicle selling medical supplies or something. Like he didn’t have that — whatever happened for you did not necessarily happen for him. Maybe it’s different for vocalists. © Fillius Jazz Archive -11-

It’s different when you are a super young vocalist. And what happened that year sort of got a lot of press too, because they changed the age limit and so the winner of the competition, Terry Thornton, was over 40 years older than I was. She was first and I was second. She was over sixty and I was twenty. So that big gap got a lot of attention. And plus I got up there and I was really confident and I had, you know, charts for the guys and was an experienced musician and had no problem doing what I was doing and…
Well thank you for leading into my next question. What do you think singers should be able to convey to their band?
